channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: ‘Roubalheira na mais alta cúpula do Judiciário', diz Flávio Bolsonaro em almoço com empresários
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL presidential candidate, accused Brazil's highest judicial authorities of 'corruption' during a lunch with businessmen in São Caetano do Sul, without providing evidence. He also claimed his opponents fear his victory and would go to 'the limit of wickedness' to stop him, adding he intends to 'resist' in the remaining 57 days before the election, citing his father Jair Bolsonaro's support.

item.title: TV Cultura terá edições especiais do Roda Viva com candidatos ao governo de SP
item.description: TV Cultura will host special Roda Viva interviews with São Paulo gubernatorial candidates Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) and Fernando Haddad (PT) on August 24 and 31, respectively, at 10 p.m., moderated by journalist Ernesto Paglia, with an identical journalist panel to ensure equal conditions.

item.title: PT protocola candidatura de Lula e plano de governo; veja pontos
item.description: The PT filed Lula’s candidacy for re-election in 2026, accompanied by a government plan focused on strengthening women’s protection, including expanding victim support services, completing Brazilian Women’s Houses, expanding Lilás Rooms, and reinforcing aggressor monitoring. The plan also promotes women’s economic autonomy through entrepreneurship incentives and pay equity. The proposal for zero-fare urban public transport was dropped from the final document due to perceived infeasibility.

item.title: Tarcísio registra candidatura e declara patrimônio de R$ 2,7 milhões
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) filed for re-election to the Palácio dos Bandeirantes, declaring a net worth of R$ 2.7 million, including R$ 525,000 in savings and a Brasília property valued at over R$ 2.1 million — nearly unchanged from his R$ 2.3 million declaration in 2022. His running mate, Felicio Ramuth (MDB), saw his assets grow from R$ 1.4 million to R$ 2.9 million, acquiring two plots of land worth R$ 1.6 million total. The candidacy was officially registered with the TSE on Friday, August 7.

item.title: Crusoé: Lula define slogan para campanha à reeleição
item.description: President Lula (PT) has defined the slogan 'Brazil ready for more' for his 2026 re-election campaign, developed with input from campaign marketer Raul Rabelo and Secretary of Social Communication Minister Sidônio Palmeira. The campaign's visual identity was also established, though specific details were not disclosed in the provided excerpt.

item.title: Dino manda investigar emendas Pix de vice de Flávio, Hugo Motta e outros parlamentares
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino ordered the Federal Police to investigate 100 Pix amendments following irregularities identified by the TCU, resulting in an estimated R$ 49 million loss to public funds. Among those mentioned are Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL), announced as Flávio Bolsonaro's vice-presidential candidate, and Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB), Chamber president, whose amendments showed lack of transparency, overpricing, and failure to account for funds. The lawmakers are not direct targets but may become subjects of investigation as the probe progresses.

item.title: Veja o que é #FATO e o que é #FAKE na entrevista de Ronaldo Caiado ao g1 e à GloboNews
item.description: In an interview with g1 and GloboNews, Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) made two statements fact-checked by Fato ou Fake: one claiming 9.1 million students had not completed high school, rated 'Not Quite True' as the figure from 2023 had dropped to 7.7 million by 2025; another stating 82% of Brazilian families are in debt, confirmed as true by the CNC. Caiado was portrayed as a presidential candidate criticizing current educational and economic conditions.

item.title: Carlos Bolsonaro declara R$ 2,7 milhões em bens e nenhum imóvel em SC
item.description: Carlos Bolsonaro (PL), Senate candidate for Santa Catarina, declared R$2.7 million in assets to the TSE, including four vehicles but no real estate in the state where he is running. The declaration highlights the absence of property ownership in SC despite the high total value of declared assets.

item.title: Atas do PL deixam brecha para Gaspar ser candidato ao Senado em caso de mudança de vice de Flávio
item.description: PL meeting minutes reveal Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL) was registered as vice-presidential candidate on Flávio Bolsonaro’s ticket while also being maintained as a Senate candidate in Alagoas, creating a loophole for his replacement on the presidential ticket until August 15, should the party decide to change the vice due to backlash over allegations of rape of a vulnerable person. The Alagoas state PL minutes delegate authority to the state executive to alter Senate candidacies, allowing Gaspar to run for Senate if removed from the presidential ticket. Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign did not comment.

item.title: Lula define slogan para campanha de 2026: “O Brasil pronto pra mais”
item.description: President Lula (PT) has defined 'Brazil ready for more' as the slogan for his 2026 re-election campaign, with input from campaign strategist Raul Rabelo and Minister of Secom Sidônio Palmeira. The campaign will feature a logo with Lula and his running mate Geraldo Alckmin, and will use a color palette that extends beyond the PT's traditional red to include green, yellow, and blue — the colors of the Brazilian flag — in an effort to reclaim national symbols historically associated with the right.

item.title: Por Dentro das Eleições: saiba as regras para reclamações, representações e direito de resposta
item.description: The 2026 General Elections in Brazil may lead to judicial disputes, including complaints, representations, and right-of-reply requests filed by political parties, the Public Prosecutor’s Office, and candidates. These matters are reviewed by auxiliary judges appointed by electoral tribunals, such as Minister Estela Aranha, President Kassio Nunes Marques, and Minister André Mendonça at the TSE. Electoral administrative complaints, special representations, and right-of-reply petitions can be submitted by any party, coalition, or candidate and must be directed to the TSE in presidential elections.

item.title: Sérgio Moro diz que Valdemar Costa Neto já pagou por ‘erros do passado’
item.description: Sérgio Moro defended Valdemar Costa Neto, stating that his past errors tied to the Mensalão scandal have already been atoned for and that he served his sentence. He dismissed the STF’s asset freeze on Costa Neto, claiming no evidence of diversion in parliamentary amendments, and emphasized his own transparent allocation of R$69 million to Paraná’s philanthropic hospitals. Moro reaffirmed his 2026 gubernatorial bid focused on security, health, education, and infrastructure, expressing concern over alleged Lula administration interference in the Federal Police.

item.title: Erika Hilton sobre bens declarados: "Impossível enriquecer sendo honesta"
item.description: Deputy Erika Hilton (PSOL-SP) defended her declared assets of R$15,975.73 to the TSE for the 2026 elections, stating it is 'impossible to get rich in politics while being honest'. She explained her salary supports her family, close ones, debt repayment, and housing allowance, criticizing the disproportionate focus on her modest wealth compared to politicians whose assets grow inexplicably.

item.title: Tarcísio de Freitas registra candidatura ao governo de SP e declara patrimônio de R$ 2,7 milhões
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) registered his candidacy for governor of São Paulo with incumbent vice-governor Felicio Ramuth (PSD) seeking re-election. The governor declared assets of R$ 2.7 million, including a Brasília property and R$ 525,000 in savings, showing minimal change from R$ 2.3 million declared in 2022. Ramuth increased his holdings from R$ 1.4 million to R$ 2.9 million, mainly through the purchase of two plots valued at R$ 825,000 and R$ 778,000 since 2022.

item.title: Vice de Renan Santos declara pistola e medalha de ouro ao TSE
item.description: Aroldo Medina, vice-presidential candidate on Renan Santos' ticket for the 2026 elections, declared assets totaling R$ 1.59 million to the TSE, including a Taurus pistol (R$ 12,000), a solid gold medal commemorating the centenary of Porto Alegre's Military College (R$ 200,000), and a military police officer's sword (R$ 10,000). His wealth is primarily real estate-based, comprising two buildings valued at R$ 750,000 and R$ 480,000, plus two vehicles. Medina is a reserve lieutenant-colonel of the Rio Grande do Sul Military Brigade and a journalist.

item.title: Mendonça manda PT entregar documentos de congresso e projeto sobre Lula
item.description: Supreme Court Justice André Mendonça ordered the Workers' Party (PT) to submit, within five days, the full recordings of its 8th National Congress and the launch event of the 'Lula's Spokespeople' project, along with contracts, invoices, and receipts. The ruling aims to investigate possible irregularities in the funding and organization of these events.

item.title: Assessor de Putin que visita o Brasil é sancionado pelos EUA
item.description: Nikolai Patrushev, an advisor to Vladimir Putin, has been under U.S. sanctions since 2018 over his role in the 2014 annexation of Crimea, and has also been sanctioned by the EU, UK, France, Japan, and others. Despite this, he is currently visiting Brazil, meeting with President Lula, Defense Minister José Múcio, and presidential advisor Celso Amorim to discuss military and diplomatic cooperation between Russia and Brazil. Brazil does not recognize unilateral sanctions and adheres only to UN-approved measures, allowing Patrushev to conduct official engagements, including a visit to the NAM Atlântico, Latin America’s largest warship.

item.title: Patrimônio de Carlos Bolsonaro cresce 40% em 2 anos e atinge R$ 2,7 milhões
item.description: Carlos Bolsonaro's declared wealth grew 40.4% over two years, rising from R$ 1.98 million in 2024 to R$ 2.78 million in 2026. The increase was primarily driven by diverse investments, now totaling R$ 1.95 million of his declared assets to the TSE. He is running for Senate in Santa Catarina in the 2026 elections.

item.title: Zema propõe privatizações, saída do BRICS e flexibilização da CLT
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) presented his 81-page government plan, 'Implacable Plan', focused on economic development, combating the 'Brazil Cost', privatization of state-owned enterprises and public assets, CLT flexibilization, and withdrawing from BRICS to join the OECD. The plan includes proposals such as the 'Partners of Brazil' program (R$ 1,000 per Brazilian at birth), gradual reduction of corporate income tax to developed-country levels, and payroll tax exemptions for formal hiring in SMEs. While detailed in general guidelines, the document lacks specificity on implementation mechanisms.

item.title: Dino manda investigar vice de Flávio após PGR arquivar o caso
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino ordered an investigation into a Pix amendment by deputy Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL), who is the pre-candidate for vice president on the ticket led by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, even after the Attorney General's Office (PGR) had archived a complaint filed by deputy Lindbergh Farias (PT). The decision comes despite the PGR's dismissal of the case, indicating a divergence in interpretation between the judicial and prosecutorial bodies. The case involves suspicions of irregularities in the allocation of public funds through parliamentary amendments.

item.title: Desmatamento na Amazônia registra novo recorde de baixa
item.description: The Legal Amazon recorded its lowest deforestation level in the last decade over the past year, confirming a downward trend observed since the beginning of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's administration. Official data released this Friday (7) indicates progress in the current government's environmental policies.

item.title: Irmão de PC Farias é indicado suplente de Arthur Lira ao Senado em AL
item.description: Luiz Romero Farias, a physician, businessman, and brother of PC Farias, was nominated by the PL as the first substitute for federal deputy Arthur Lira's (PP) Senate candidacy in Alagoas. The information appears in the party convention minutes submitted to the TSE last night.

item.title: Lula diz que secretário de Trump é ‘latino-americano frustrado’ e ‘odeia o Brasil’
item.description: President Lula accused U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio of being a 'frustrated Latin American' who hates Brazil and other Latin American countries, amid escalating bilateral tensions. The remarks followed the U.S. revocation of the visa of Brazilian ambassador Maria Luiza Viotti, in retaliation for Brazil's delay in accepting Trump's nominee Daniel Perez, an ally of Rubio, as the new U.S. ambassador to Brazil. Lula called the U.S. action 'false' and announced diplomatic reciprocity.

item.title: Lula chama Rubio de “latino-americano frustrado” e “bolsonarista”
item.description: President Lula called U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio a 'frustrated Latin American' and a 'bolsonarist' during a visit to INPE in São José dos Campos. He made the remarks while criticizing U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods, claiming Rubio dislikes Brazil and Latin America. Lula linked Rubio’s stance to sympathy with Bolsonarism.

item.title: Governo Lula avalia que aprovação de nome de embaixador dos EUA pelo Senado não muda cenário sobre aval diplomático
item.description: The Lula government says the U.S. Senate's approval of Daniel Perez as ambassador to Brazil does not change the diplomatic stalemate, as Itamaraty still must approve his nomination. Brazil views the U.S. pressure as 'blackmail' and will not grant agrément until after the October elections, seeing the revocation of Ambassador Maria Luiza Viotti's visa as a complete breakdown in talks. While uncomfortable with the reversed diplomatic protocol, Lula's allies rule out immediate retaliation, viewing the move as a potential trap to provoke Brazil into escalating the conflict.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro oficializa Sanderson ao Senado pelo RS
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), presidential candidate for 2026, officially endorsed the candidacies of Sanderson (PL) and Marcel van Hattem (Novo) for the two Senate seats in Rio Grande do Sul. The announcement was made during a live broadcast, reinforcing the PL-Novo alliance in the state.

item.title: Mendonça determina que PT entregue documentos do congresso da sigla e do projeto Porta-Vozes de Lula
item.description: TSE Justice André Mendonça ordered the PT to submit, within five days, full recordings of its 8th National Congress and the launch of the 'Porta-Vozes de Lula' project, along with contracts, invoices, payment proofs, and accounting documents related to these events. The ruling aims to ensure transparency and oversight of party expenditures.

item.title: Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro não participam de entrevistas do g1 e da GloboNews com candidatos à Presidência
item.description: President Lula (PT) and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) will not participate in the g1 and GloboNews interview series with presidential candidates, after Lula's campaign declined the invitation for Tuesday (4) and Flávio's campaign failed to respond in time. Interviews with Renan Santos (Missão), Romeu Zema (Novo), and Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) proceeded as scheduled, featuring the five top candidates from the July 24 Datafolha poll. The interviews were conducted by journalists Andréia Sadi and Natuza Nery in GloboNews' new studios in Rio de Janeiro.

item.title: PP oficializa candidatura de Janaína Paschoal para deputada federal
item.description: The Progressistas (PP) officially nominated councilwoman Janaína Paschoal as their federal deputy candidate, with registration filed at the Electoral Justice on Friday (August 7). The party had been urging her to run for weeks, viewing her as a potential vote-getter. Paschoal was elected São Paulo councilwoman in 2024 with 48,900 votes and gained national prominence as one of the authors of the impeachment request against Dilma Rousseff; in 2018, she became the most-voted deputy in Brazilian history, securing over two million votes for the São Paulo State Assembly (Alesp).

item.title: 20 anos da Lei Maria da Penha: Justiça Eleitoral amplia proteção a candidatas e eleitoras
item.description: Brazil's Electoral Justice is intensifying efforts to protect female candidates and voters from gender-based violence, extending the reach of the Maria da Penha Law to the political sphere. The TSE and regional electoral courts are strengthening specialized channels, such as the Women's Ombudsman, to receive complaints of harassment and discrimination, ensuring confidentiality and swift referral to competent authorities. The August Lilac campaign gains strategic focus in 2026, bringing domestic safety and dignity guarantees into the public arena of power.

item.title: Lula chama Rubio de "latino-americano frustrado": “Ele odeia o Brasil”
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva criticized U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, calling him a 'frustrated Latin American' and claiming he 'hates Brazil'. Lula noted that despite efforts to engage in dialogue during his meeting with Donald Trump at the White House, no positive response followed, and the U.S. subsequently imposed high tariffs on Brazilian goods. The remarks come amid rising bilateral tensions, including the suspension of the Brazilian ambassador's visa in Washington.

item.title: Zema propõe saída dos Brics, privatizações e R$ 1 mil para cada brasileiro ao nascer
item.description: Romeu Zema, the Novo party's presidential candidate, proposes privatizing all state-owned companies, depositing R$1,000 for every Brazilian newborn, and paying a R$5,000 bonus to families with children. He also advocates for Brazil's withdrawal from the BRICS bloc as part of his economic and foreign policy agenda.

item.title: Alertas em desmatamento caem e Lula critica Trump: 'Mandar foto para ele'
item.description: Following a decline in deforestation alerts in the Amazon, President Lula said he wants to take a photo of the data to send to U.S. President Donald Trump, in response to American tariffs on Brazilian goods justified by deforestation concerns. Lula indirectly criticized the U.S. trade policy, implying that improved environmental data should be acknowledged.

item.title: Patrimônio de Júlia Zanatta mais que dobra em 4 anos. Veja os bens
item.description: The net worth of federal deputy Júlia Zanatta (PL-SC) more than doubled between 2022 and 2024, rising from R$ 2.525 million to R$ 5.187 million, an increase of approximately 105%. The growth is primarily attributed to land, real estate, and financial investments, including R$ 85,000 in cash. The declaration was submitted to the TSE in her 2024 candidacy registration.

item.title: Eleição presidencial: as propostas de Zema que têm potencial para causar polêmica
item.description: Romeu Zema's (Novo) 2026 presidential government plan advocates radical liberal measures, including the privatization of Petrobras, Caixa Econômica Federal and Banco do Brasil, abolition of public electoral financing, and labor flexibility allowing workdays over 8 hours daily under a voluntary parallel regime to CLT. The plan, dubbed 'Implacable Plan,' also increases surveillance and toughens criminal legislation. These proposals require constitutional changes and congressional approval, facing strong opposition from political parties, unions, and sectors viewing state enterprises as strategic.

item.title: EUA sobre tensão diplomática com Brasil: “Situação não nos interessa”
item.description: The U.S. government stated that the diplomatic crisis with Brazil over the delay in approving Daniel Perez as ambassador 'does not interest' the United States, but emphasized its commitment to preserving bilateral relations, respecting the Brazilian people and governments chosen in free and fair elections. Despite criticism of the Lula administration, Washington avoided framing the impasse as a rupture, highlighting the importance of trade, investment, and cultural ties between the two nations.

item.title: TSE cria conselho para monitorar desinformação e uso de IA durante as eleições de 2026
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) established the Advisory Council on Informational Integrity for the 2026 Elections to monitor disinformation and improper use of AI during campaigns. The council, composed of volunteer experts in technology, communication, and public security, will advise the TSE president on studies and recommendations to strengthen electoral integrity, following the deepfake incident involving Jair Bolsonaro at the PL party convention.

item.title: Talíria Petrone denuncia ameaça de morte, ataque a filhos e divulgação de dados pessoais
item.description: Federal deputy Talíria Petrone (PSOL-RJ) reported receiving a new death and rape threat via email, which disclosed her personal data and that of her family, including explicit threats against her children. This marks the third such incident in recent months, prompting referrals to the Federal Police, Legislative Police, MPF, PPDDH, and TSE due to the electoral context. Petrone emphasized that the message also contained misogynistic insults and attacks on her political work defending women's and Black people's rights.

item.title: Papo Antagonista: quem são os políticos que lideram as vaquinhas nesta eleição?
item.description: The Papo Antagonista on Friday, the 7th, analyzed the candidates who raised the most money through the crowdfunding platform 'QueroApoiar' in the 2026 elections. The TSE regulated crowdfunding for political campaigns in 2017, enabling this fundraising method. The segment highlighted the top fundraisers via vaquinhas as an indicator of grassroots support and campaign strategy.

item.title: Após aprovação de Daniel Perez pelo Senado dos EUA, governo Lula mantém posição de analisar indicação depois das eleições
item.description: The Lula government maintains its stance of waiting until after Brazil's 2026 presidential elections to analyze the nomination of Daniel Perez as U.S. ambassador to Brazil, viewing the U.S. Senate's approval as part of a pressure campaign. Brazil's refusal to grant agrément immediately is seen as a response to the lack of prior consultation by the U.S. and the revocation of the Brazilian ambassador's visa in Washington, which has deepened the diplomatic crisis.

item.title: Boulos questiona “autoridade moral” da oposição para criticar Lulinha
item.description: Guilherme Boulos, Minister of the General Secretariat of the Presidency, defended Fábio Luís Lula da Silva (Lulinha), son of President Lula, who is under investigation for alleged diversion of INSS pensions. Boulos downplayed the impact of the suspicions and questioned the 'moral authority' of the opposition to criticize the case, suggesting the accusations are politically motivated.

item.title: Lula diz que mandará para Trump "foto" da queda de desmatamento
item.description: President Lula said he will visit INPE to take a photo of Brazil's deforestation decline data and send it to Donald Trump. He criticized U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio as a Bolsonarist and anti-Latino-American, noting that despite a meeting with Trump at the White House, the U.S. imposed additional tariffs on Brazilian goods.

item.title: Lula chama Marco Rubio de ‘bolsonarista’ e ‘anti-latino-americano’
item.description: President Lula called U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio a 'bolsonarista' and 'anti-Latin American', accusing him of acting against agreements with Donald Trump and denying the climate crisis. Lula said he provided documents on trade, organized crime, and rare earths to the U.S. to ease tensions but is still awaiting a response. He also rejected Trump’s justification for 25% tariffs on Brazilian exports, asserting Brazil’s stronger environmental commitment.

item.title: Ao registrar candidatura para presidente, Renan Santos declara R$ 759.000 em bens
item.description: Renan Santos, the presidential candidate from the Missão party, declared R$ 759,000 in assets, making him the third candidate to have his data disclosed by the TSE in 2026. His main assets are credits and savings (R$ 300,000), followed by assets related to self-employment (R$ 275,329). Meanwhile, Romeu Zema emerged as the wealthiest presidential candidate with R$ 178.7 million in assets, while Hertz Dias (PSTU) declared no assets.

item.title: EUA descartam rompimento com o Brasil: “Não nos interessa”
item.description: The U.S. government ruled out the possibility of severing diplomatic ties with Brazil, stating it will respect the outcome of free and fair elections in the country. The statement was made in response to speculation about bilateral tensions, reinforcing that the partnership with Brazil is considered important. The U.S. emphasized that it respects the Brazilian people and any government democratically elected.

item.title: Renan Santos declara patrimônio de R$ 795 mil ao registrar candidatura à Presidência no TSE
item.description: Renan Santos, presidential candidate for the Missão party, declared assets of R$ 795,000 to the TSE, including capital quotas, corporate stakes, assets related to autonomous activity, and savings or credit. In his speech, he criticized Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, advocating 'kill those who steal'. According to the Genial/Quaest poll, he has 4% of voting intentions in the first round, while Lula leads with 40% and Flávio Bolsonaro with 28%.

item.title: Missão oficializa 128 candidaturas para deputado e deixa em aberto apoio a governo e Senado por SP
item.description: The Mission party officially registered 128 candidacies for the 2026 proportional elections: 71 for state deputy and 57 for federal deputy, including 28 women for the São Paulo State Legislature and 21 for the Chamber of Deputies. While it has nominated Renan Santos for president, the party has not yet decided whether to run or support candidates for governor of São Paulo and senator, with the decision still under analysis. Party conventions could be held until August 5, with candidate registration at the Electoral Justice allowed until August 15.

item.title: Flávio critica Judiciário e diz haver tentativa de barrar sua eleição
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL party's presidential candidate, criticized the judiciary and claimed there is a movement to prevent his election, denouncing alleged corruption in public administration and asserting that opponents would go to extreme lengths to block him. He also criticized President Lula, arguing that the PT leader had three terms to improve the country and would fail in a fourth, while promising a 'modern' and future-oriented government. Bolsonaro stated he fears no new accusations, saying his life has already been investigated without finding any wrongdoing.

item.title: Big techs reduzem medidas para eleição e encaram novas regras judiciais no Brasil
item.description: Big techs face an unprecedented scenario in Brazil's 2026 elections, compelled to comply with new judicial rulings while following U.S.-based parent company directives to reduce content moderation and prioritize free speech. This tension between local regulation and global corporate policy creates uncertainty for digital platforms operating in Brazil.

item.title: Dino manda PF investigar emendas Pix de vice de Flávio, Motta e ex-líder do PT após auditoria do TCU
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino ordered the Federal Police to investigate alleged crimes in the execution of R$55.4 million in Pix amendments, following a TCU audit. The amendments are linked to Dino’s vice, deputy Motta, and a former PT leader. The case raises suspicions of public fund diversion and is being treated as a potential corruption scheme.
